Title: Diagnosis of test `test_getShortClassName_Class`

Details:
The test `test_getShortClassName_Class` fails on the assertion that the short class name of `String[].class` should be `"String[]"`. The failure suggests that the method `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)` does not correctly handle array classes.

Examining the code of `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)`, we see it simply calls `getShortClassName(String)` on the class's name obtained by `cls.getName()`. This delegates the actual name extraction to `getShortClassName(String)`.

In the `getShortClassName(String)` method, the input fully qualified class name string is processed by:
- Returning an empty string if null or empty.
- Then some comments hinting at handling array encoding and stripping object type encoding, but no actual code is observed related to these steps.
- It extracts the substring after the last package separator `'.'` and handles inner class separator characters by replacing them with `'.'`.
- Finally, it returns the substring extracted.

The bug originates because `getShortClassName(String)` does not properly handle array class name encodings. The class name of `String[].class` in JVM internal representation is something like `[Ljava.lang.String;`. The method `getShortClassName(String)` treats it as a normal class name and does not convert this array syntax to a short readable class name like `"String[]"`.

Therefore, the test fails because the returned string is not `"String[]"` but something else derived from the raw internal class name with the array encoding present.

This analysis shows that the failure comes from `getShortClassName(String)` lacking the logic to decode array class name representations into the human-readable short class names expected.

Suggested methods to fix:
- `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)`
- Possibly `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.Class<?>)` if additional handling is to be done at this level

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
